author: Erik Berlin
description: Duel runs your benchmarks on two versions of your code side by side, the baseline (where your branch left main, say) and the candidate, and fails if the candidate is slower at any of them. Timings are judged by a distribution-free confidence interval for paired CPU-time ratios and confirmed in fres…

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: every benchmark is judged on the SQL queries, cached queries, transactions and record instantiations Active Record did for it too, whatever the database.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin for Rails apps: each version of the app booted like production, with its own bundle and database, and benchmarks of its requests, judged on time, allocations, queries, views and cache use.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: each worker gets a PostgreSQL server of its own, and every benchmark is judged on the queries it sent, the rows they returned, the buffers they touched and their time too.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: each worker gets a MySQL server of its own, and every benchmark is judged on the statements it sent, the rows they read and their time too.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: each worker gets a Redis server of its own, and every benchmark is judged on the Redis CPU time, commands and round trips it took too.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: each worker gets a memcached server of its own, and every benchmark is judged on the memcached operations, misses and bytes it took too.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: benchmarks with threads of their own are judged on how long their threads waited for the GVL too, so a change that adds contention fails even when its CPU time doesn't.

author: Erik Berlin
description: A Duel plugin: every benchmark is judged on the Ruby objects its iterations leave alive after a full garbage collection, so a leak, or a cache that grows with every call, fails.

author: iagus
description: Opf fetches OpenGraph metadata (title, description, images) and the favicon URL from user-provided URLs, raising typed errors for invalid URLs or failed fetches.
